text: I went back over it, which is the part of the job where you find out how little you have.

pay: That was how little I had. It was more than nothing, and I’ve worked with nothing.

text: I found a quiet corner and went over what I had. It didn’t take as long as I’d have liked.

pay: I got up out of the quiet corner. It had been the most restful part of the night, and it was over.

text: I sat back and went over it.
I stood where I was and went through the notebook from the top.
I took the notebook out and went over it from the top, slowly, because slowly is the only speed it has.

pay: I shut the notebook. It had gone as fast as it goes, which is not fast.

text: I stopped and took stock. Taking stock is free, which is the best thing I can say about it.

pay: Taking stock had cost me nothing, and it was worth every cent.

text: It was getting late, and late is when you count what you’ve got.

pay: That was the count. It hadn’t taken long, which left more of the night to add to it.

text: Another hour had gone, and I went over what it had bought me.

figure.text: what the hour had bought me
figure.short: what the hour had bought me
pay: That was what the hour had bought me. I’ve paid more for less.

text: Somebody’s story had come apart, and that’s a good time to go over all the others.

pay: The other stories were still in one piece. I handled them a little more carefully after that.

text: Now I had two versions of one half hour, and I went back over the rest to see what else wobbled.

pay: Nothing else wobbled yet. I gave it time.

text: When somebody changes a story, you check all the other ones. I went over what I had.

pay: The other stories were standing where I’d left them, which is all you can ask of a story that late in the night.

text: I let that settle and went back over it from the top.
The hour that mattered had got smaller, and I went over everything else against it.

pay: The hour that mattered was smaller than it had been. So, by then, was my patience.

text: Now I knew when better than I had, and I went over the rest with that in mind.
I had put a name to a face, in pencil, and that called for going over everything else.

figure.text: a name put to a face in pencil
pay: The name was still in pencil. I keep an eraser for exactly that, and I’ve worn out three.

text: That was the night so far: a lot of people who were somewhere, and one half hour nobody was keen to talk about.
That was where things stood. It wasn’t far, but it was further than the police had got.
That was it. It fitted on one page of the notebook, which is either good news or bad.
That was the whole of it, as of now. It’s always the whole of it, as of now.
That was the night so far, laid out flat.
That was what I had. None of it was a name yet, and I wasn’t going to pretend otherwise.
I got the notebook out and read it back to myself, which is as close as anybody comes to reading me a story.

pay: I put the notebook away. It hadn’t told me anything I hadn’t told it first.

text: I stopped where I was and read the notebook from the first page, moving my lips only a little.

figure.text: my lips, moving only a little
pay: I put the notebook away and stopped moving my lips.

text: Another hour had gone by without asking me, so I went over what I had to show for it.

figure.text: what I had to show for it
figure.short: what I had to show for it
pay: That was what I had to show for it. I’ve shown less and got away with it.

text: One story had just turned into a different one. When that happens, I count all the others again.

figure.text: all the other stories, counted again
pay: The others all counted out the same as before. I counted them twice, to be sure of it.

text: I had put something to somebody and got something back. I went over the rest while it was still warm.

figure.text: the rest, while it was still warm
pay: It had all cooled a little by the time I was done. So had I.

text: The time that mattered was narrower now, and I held everybody’s evening up against it.
I had a name and a face that might go together. I went over the rest before I got attached.

pay: I wasn’t attached yet. I’ve been attached before, and it ended in a lot of apologies.

text: The night was getting on, and so was I. I sat down and went over what I had.

pay: The night went on getting on. I got up and went with it.

text: I stopped and added it up, which is the arithmetic part of the job and the part I’m worst at.

figure.text: the arithmetic part of the job
pay: That was the sum of it. I checked my arithmetic, and it was still the sum of it.

text: I leaned on the nearest wall and went through the notebook. The wall had the easier job.

pay: I came off the wall. It had held up its end, and I meant to hold up mine.
